EA-006.previous_note: Line and Arrow preserve ordered endpoints (direction), optional curved control geometry, border style (solid/dash/dot/dashDot/dashDotDot), thickness, arrow style (classic/modern/double/basic/line), shadow and opacity through bounded XANN read/write (unknown fields kept, older documents load at defaults and re-serialize byte-identically), one shared paintShape path for canvas and export, one-undo-step native edit dialog, session creation defaults, copy/paste/duplicate, move and resize. Decisions: (1) borderStyle, shadow* reuse the EA-005 names, values and defaults, which follow the reference XerahS Annotation.cs/LineAnnotation.cs/BorderStyle.cs; the reference Arrow has no borderStyle, so Arrow also accepts it (dashes the shaft, head stays solid) because EA-006 lists border style for both. (2) Arrow style is persisted as `style` with camelCase values classic/modern/double/basic/line, read case-insensitively, as in reference ArrowAnnotation.cs/ArrowStyle.cs; head geometry and size multipliers (2.0 classic/double, 3.0 modern, 1.75 basic/line, length 3x) follow the reference, so head size is derived from thickness and has no field; Modern is straight and drops the curve, as in the reference CurvedSegmentHelper. (3) The reference stores the curve as `curvePoint` {x,y} in document pixels plus `curvePointActivated` (a point the quadratic passes through at its middle). Here it is the optional third entry of the fractional `points`, so move/resize/flip and the shared all-annotation transform carry it with the endpoints; reference curvePoint/curvePointActivated are accepted on read and converted. Writes use points[2]. Lines or arrows with more than 3 points remain legacy polylines. Curve anchor fractions are bounded to +-1e6. (4) Shadow, ranges and the 1px minimum box follow EA-005. Open: no on-canvas curve drag handle yet (curve is edited in the properties dialog); golden pixels for arrow heads are not contract-defined.

Audit 2026-11-03: Alphabetic (upper/lower), Roman (upper/lower), explicit start number and reset are implemented per the reference XerahS source, which Mike's standing rule makes the tie-breaker where the contract is silent: StepType.cs StepTypeFormatter (alphabetic is bijective base 26: 1=A, 26=Z, 27=AA, case per style; values <= 0 print as plain decimal; Roman is standard subtractive with M repeated above 3999, so 4000=MMMM), MainViewModel.ToolOptions (start number 1..10, default 1, out-of-range clamps) and MainViewModel.RecalculateNumberCounter (next = max(highest+1, start)). Proving tests: AnnotationShapesTest::stepStylesMapValuesLikeTheReference (0, -5, 1, 4, 9, 26, 27, 52, 702, 703, 1994, 3999, 4000), ::stepStyleNamesFollowTheReferenceSpelling, ::stepStyleRoundTripsPerObjectAndRejectsUnknownNames, ::stepStartAndResetAffectOnlyFutureAllocation, ::stepValuesStayStableAcrossDeleteReorderUndoRedoAndReload, ::stepStyleIsOneUndoableContentEditAndPaintsTheFormattedLabel; EditorCanvasTest::stepCreationUsesSavedStyleStartAndResetAndEditChangesOnlyTheSelectedStep; EditorPreferencesTest::everyReferenceStepStyleIsImplementedAndReachesCreationDefaults; NativeEditorPreferencesTest::missingSavedFontFallsBackWithoutRewritingUntilExplicitReplacement (unknown style stays inert). Decision: points[0] is the tail tip as a fraction of the step's box (as for the speech balloon, so move, resize, flip, rotate, cut-out and copy carry it); no point means no tail, which is the reference state before a tail point is set and the creation default (reference creates steps without a tail point); a present point is TailEnabled+initialized, so the reference enabled-but-uninitialized and disabled-but-initialized states collapse (rationale: one persisted field, no hidden state). The tail is the two tangents from the tip to the circle, drawn as one silhouette with the circle (reference TryGetTailPolygon); a tip on or inside the circle draws none. Default tip when enabling in the dialog is (1.5, 1.5), the reference default handle one radius beyond the bottom-right corner. Proving tests: AnnotationShapesTest::stepTailRendersPersistsAndIsOneUndoableEdit and ::stepTailRejectsInvalidTipsWithoutChangingHistoryOrDocuments; EditorCanvasTest::stepTailIsEditedThroughTheStepDialogInOneUndoStep; with the existing numeric/alphabetic/Roman, start, reset and stability tests every EA-009 clause now has a named test.

EA-011.note: Region effect geometry/ellipse/blur fields are typed and rendered from immutable source; source-only blur and moved Pixelate scenarios are tested.

EA-011.previous_note: Highlight, Blur, Pixelate, Magnify and Spotlight apply only inside their declared geometry and read only the immutable source image (ShapePainter.cpp effectRegion/paintRegion/paintHighlight/paintMagnify/paintSpotlight; canvas preview and exporter share paintShape). Options follow the reference XANN format (camelCase, defaults omitted on write, unknown fields preserved, bounded validation): `isEllipse` (bool, default false = rectangle) on all five types, Spotlight `blurAmount` (0..1000, default 0) blurring the dimmed area, plus the existing `strength`. Rationale per field: isEllipse = reference BaseEffectAnnotation/SpotlightAnnotation.IsEllipse and ImageEditorOptions.MagnifierEllipse/SpotlightEllipse; blurAmount = reference SpotlightAnnotation.BlurAmount / ImageEditorOptions.SpotlightBlur (reference default 0); Blur has no blur-type option in the reference so none is invented; Highlight/Blur/Pixelate use IsEllipse as in the reference (Highlight has no strength). Persisted strength keeps this build's `strength` name on write. Reference compatibility (read-only aliases, used only when `strength` is absent, consumed so they are not preserved beside `strength`): Blur/Pixelate/Magnify `amount` (0..1000) is read as `strength`, and Spotlight `darkenOpacity` (reference byte 0..255) is read as `strength` percent = darkenOpacity/2.55 (Spotlight strength is the dim percentage, alpha = percent*2.55; 0 maps to 0.01 because strength 0 means the default); out-of-range or non-numeric aliases are rejected like `strength`; an unrelated `amount` on Spotlight/Highlight and an `amount` beside an explicit `strength` stay verbatim. EffectRegionTest::referenceAmountAndDarkenOpacityAreReadAsStrengthAliasesAndWrittenAsStrength covers it. Behaviour changes: Spotlight is now rectangular unless isEllipse is set (reference default; it was always elliptical before), and Magnify no longer draws a stroke border outside its region. A rotated region samples the source under the rotated outline (previously the unrotated box was rotated). Effects replace pixels inside the region from the source, so overlapping effects never see each other's output; Spotlight's dim is an overlay and its blur samples the source. Native: the existing strength dialog gains an Elliptical region checkbox (Highlight: a Rectangle/Ellipse choice) and, for Spotlight, a blur spin box; one Apply is one history operation; unchanged Apply records nothing. Ellipse hit-testing excludes the corners. EffectRegionTest covers rect/ellipse x rotated masks for all five effects, edge clipping incl. 1e9 extents and off-canvas regions, blur position independence, overlap/reorder against the immutable source, repaint independence from canvas contents, canvas==export pixels, byte determinism, XANN round-trip incl. a hand-written reference-style document, invalid option rejection, and native edit/cancel/undo/redo/reload. Independent human visual qualification on target distributions is a release-level activity and is not part of this clause set.

An asset-bearing clipboard payload is version 2: the annotations plus an assets object carrying the base64 PNG of exactly the referenced Image/Emoji/Cursor keys (asset-free copies stay version 1; unselected assets are never included).
